cards.explanation: The answer is commandments. Jesus tells the man, “If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.” That's the whole answer, and it fits on one line, which is more than I can say for my recipe cards. He says it right after telling the man, “There is only One who is good.” (Matthew 19:17)

The answer is love your neighbor as yourself. Jesus finishes the list with “…and love your neighbor as yourself.” Say it with me, friends: even the neighbor whose leaf blower fires up at 7 a.m. Jesus doesn't add that part, that's just me having fun. The list that started with “Do not murder…” lands right on loving your neighbor.

The answer is True. The young man says, “All these I have kept…” I think that's a man who feels pretty sure of himself. I once told my oven timer I'd never scorch another batch, and the timer just stayed quiet. Then he asks Jesus another question, and that's where the story really starts moving.

The answer is “What do I still lack?” After saying he has kept the commandments, that's what the young man asks Jesus. I think that's a man who has checked every box and still feels a little draft in the room. That's an honest thing to ask out loud. And Jesus gives him a direct answer.

The answer is treasure in heaven. Jesus says, “…and you will have treasure in heaven.” Notice He doesn't just say what to let go of, He says what comes next. Then He adds, “Then come, follow Me.” For the record, my own treasure is a gold base and a mustache, and I'm doing fine.

The answer is follow. Jesus says, “Then come, follow Me.” That's the invitation sitting right at the end of the instruction. It isn't only about what gets sold, friends. It's also about who he'd be walking with.

The answer is sorrow. The text says the young man “…went away in sorrow…” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story. He came up to Jesus with a big question and left with a heavy heart. I think this one hurts.

The answer is that he had great wealth. The passage says he went away in sorrow “…because he had great wealth.” That's the reason the text gives, and it doesn't add any others. Jesus had just told him to sell his possessions and give to the poor. I think that's a lot to hold in two hands.

The answer is True. The text says, “…they were greatly astonished…” Greatly, not a little. I picture a whole group going quiet at the same time, like someone just announced the oven's been off all day. Then they ask Jesus a question.

The answer is “Who then can be saved?” That's what the disciples ask after Jesus talks about the rich. That's what a group of astonished people says when the ground just moved. I think they're asking it out loud because everyone's thinking it. And Jesus looks right at them to answer.

The answer is that with God all things are possible. Jesus says, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” He's answering a question about who can be saved. It puts all the weight on God, not on us. That's good news, friends, for anybody who feels like the job is too big to do alone.

The answer is that they will judge the twelve tribes of Israel. Jesus says the disciples “…will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.” That's quite the promotion for a group that just heard a camel and a needle in the same sentence. He says it will happen in the renewal of all things. Twelve thrones is a big seating chart.

The answer is eternal. Jesus says everyone who has left those things for His name “…will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.” The hundredfold is big, and eternal life comes right alongside it. It's the same eternal life the young man asked about at the start. The story comes back around to it.

The answer is False. The second half is different from what the card says. Jesus says, “But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.” The last don't stay last, friends, they end up first. I'd say that's the part worth underlining.
